clue.text: Wrong again, by gum!

parts.note: re- is the prefix meaning again, as in redo
a sin is a wrong, a moral offence

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in exasperation at being mistaken a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By gum!' reads as a mild oath, but 'gum' is the definition and 'by' only links it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Resin is a sticky tree exudate, a kind of natural gum.

clue.text: Before autumn, pop is a danger to mountaineers

indicators.note: before means the pop word goes ahead of the autumn word in the down entry

parts.note: rock is a kind of popular music
fall is the American word for autumn

explanation.surface: Popular music arriving before the season changes threatens climbers.
explanation.definitionFit: A rockfall is a mass of loose stones tumbling down a slope, a hazard for climbers.

clue.text: Brewed ales nor Italian port

indicators.note: brewed means the letters of ales nor are mixed up like beer ingredients

explanation.surface: Neither home-brewed beer nor the Italian harbour is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Salerno is a harbour city on Italy's south-west coast.

clue.text: Coward's name for Christmas

explanation.surface: What a famous playwright calls the festive season.
explanation.walkthrough: Noel Coward was a celebrated English playwright; 'for' links the two readings.
explanation.definitionFit: Coward's first name was Noel, and noel is also a word for Christmas.

clue.text: He is not far off being a Jack of all trades

parts.note: handy means close by, within easy reach
a he is a man, a male person

explanation.surface: Someone is described as nearly a versatile worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A handyman does odd jobs of every kind, the very picture of a versatile worker.

clue.text: Range across Morocco to find high spots mapped

parts.note: something mapped appears in an atlas, a book of maps
mountains are the high spots of a landscape

explanation.surface: Peaks across a North African country can be found on a map.
explanation.definitionFit: The Atlas range runs through Morocco, Algeria and Tunisia.

clue.text: A stupid fellow might sniff it

definitions.text: A stupid fellow might sniff it

parts.words: A stupid fellow might sniff it
parts.note: a word meaning a fool which is also a drug taken up the nose

explanation.surface: Something a foolish person might inhale.
explanation.definitionFit: A dope is a dimwit; dope is also slang for drugs, some of which are snorted.

clue.text: Stroll for the cockney and his girl

parts.note: the cockney referring to himself says me
his girl is her, which a cockney says with the h dropped

explanation.surface: A leisurely walk for a Londoner and his sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: A cockney (a working-class Londoner) drops his aitches, so 'me and her' becomes 'me an' 'er'.
explanation.definitionFit: To meander is to wander in a winding, unhurried way.

clue.text: Economic council popularly called an ass

explanation.surface: A government body nicknamed a donkey.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Economic Development Council (NEDC), a former British planning body, was nicknamed Neddy.
explanation.definitionFit: Neddy was the NEDC's nickname, and a neddy is also a donkey in British slang.

clue.text: Good reason to trot German guns all over the place

indicators.note: all over the place means the letters of trot German guns are scattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: A case for marching German artillery everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong argument is a compelling case or justification.

clue.text: Get together for prayer

explanation.surface: An invitation to gather for worship.
explanation.definitionFit: To collect is to gather or assemble; a collect is also a short liturgical prayer said in church services.

clue.text: Country boy takes in the scheme

indicators.note: takes in means the boy's word holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: a lad is a boy
a plan is a scheme

explanation.surface: A rural youngster absorbs the plot being hatched.
explanation.definitionFit: Lapland is the northern region of Scandinavia, a country in the sense of a land or territory.

clue.text: Business unlikely to yield

explanation.surface: A company that will not give ground in negotiations.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm is a company; firm also means solid or resolute, not giving way under pressure.

clue.text: How cyclists go down to the seaside?

explanation.surface: A question about how riders get down the hill to the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: Cyclists coast downhill, freewheeling without pedalling; 'to the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To coast is to freewheel downhill; the coast is the shore by the sea.

clue.text: Whirl around young Edward

explanation.surface: A boy called Edward spins in circles.
explanation.definitionFit: An eddy is a swirling current of water or air; Eddy is also a pet form of the name Edward.

clue.text: Where in Florida I'm upset over a French friend

indicators.note: over means the first piece sits above the second in the down entry
upset in a down clue means the word I'm is turned upside down, reading upwards

parts.note: ami is French for friend

explanation.surface: A traveller in a US state is distressed about a pal from France.
explanation.definitionFit: Miami is a major city in Florida.

clue.text: Studies steamship about to draw up

indicators.note: about means the steamship letters go round the other piece
up in a down clue means the word for draw reads upwards

parts.note: to tow is to draw or pull along

explanation.surface: A steamer is about to be hauled up for inspection.
explanation.definitionFit: To swot is British slang for to study hard, so swots means crams.

clue.text: Anticipating what the lost walking-patient is doing?

definitions.text: what the lost walking-patient is doing?

explanation.surface: Asks what a hospital patient who has wandered off is up to.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the second reading as 'looking for ward': the lost patient is searching for the hospital ward.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking forward means awaiting eagerly; a patient lost in a hospital is looking for (his) ward.

clue.text: Pen thrown across the Nile?

parts.note: a pen is a female swan and also an enclosure; thrown across a river, a barrier holds water back

explanation.surface: A writing implement is tossed over Egypt's great river.
explanation.walkthrough: Pen means a female swan, and a dam is thrown across a river; the Aswan barrier spans the Nile in Egypt.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aswan Dam is the great barrage across the Nile.

clue.text: How, and with what, those forging ahead should be working

definitions.text: How, and with what, those forging ahead should be working

parts.words: How, and with what, those forging ahead should be working
parts.note: a blacksmith at the forge strikes with a hammer and holds the metal with tongs, and doing something vigorously is described by the phrase

explanation.surface: Advice on how keen go-getters ought to get the job done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forging ahead' suggests progress, but literally it is blacksmiths at work, whose tools give the phrase meaning 'with great energy'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means vigorously, and literally names a smith's two tools.

clue.text: Cockney bank robber's demand in Hampshire

definitions.note: the definition names the town by where it is

indicators.note: a cockney drops the h at the start of words

parts.note: a robber demands that the cashier hand over the money

explanation.surface: A London crook's demand at a bank in a southern county.
explanation.walkthrough: Hampshire is a county in southern England; a cockney is a working-class Londoner known for dropping aitches.
explanation.definitionFit: Andover is a market town in Hampshire.

clue.text: Denied Norman English initially was confined to college

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of Norman and of English

parts.note: gated is the Oxbridge term for a student confined to college as punishment

explanation.surface: An Englishman named Norman was kept in at university.
explanation.definitionFit: Negated means nullified or contradicted, much as a claim refused is denied.

clue.text: Way a dome is constructed

indicators.note: is constructed suggests the letters of the word dome are built into a new form

explanation.surface: A description of how a domed roof gets built.
explanation.definitionFit: A mode is a manner or method of doing something.

clue.text: Germinated barley on a Mediterranean island

parts.note: malt is grain, usually barley, allowed to sprout then dried for brewing

explanation.surface: Sprouting grain grown on a sunny island.
explanation.definitionFit: Malta is an island nation south of Sicily.

clue.text: Asiatic vandal taking in mother is not beastly

indicators.note: taking in means the vandal's word swallows the mother's word inside it

parts.note: the Huns were Asiatic nomads, a byword for destructive barbarians
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A barbarian invader takes in his mother and proves not to be a brute after all.
explanation.definitionFit: Being human is the opposite of being an animal or brute.

clue.text: Mogul capital provides silver god

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
Ra is the Egyptian sun god

explanation.surface: An old imperial city supplies precious metal and a deity.
explanation.walkthrough: Agra in India was the capital of the Mughal emperors and is home to the Taj Mahal.
explanation.definitionFit: Agra was the seat of the Mughal empire under several emperors.

clue.text: Disc of the new moon

definitions.note: a disc here is a gramophone record recorded on one channel

indicators.note: new means the letters of moon are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: The bright circle of the new moon in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: A mono is a record made with single-channel sound rather than stereo.

clue.text: A mother and father to all

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother

explanation.surface: A parent described as both mother and father to everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, the first man is the ancestor of all humanity.

clue.text: Having won the first courting, be faithful!

explanation.surface: Advice to a suitor who has succeeded at the first attempt to stay loyal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Courting' means on court: in tennis a server who has won the first game leads one game to love.
explanation.definitionFit: A tennis score of one game to nil is read 'love-one' from the trailing player's side; to love one person is to be faithful.

clue.text: The way first class tourer worked out

parts.note: A1 means first class, written with I standing for the figure one

indicators.note: worked out means the letters of the word tourer are rearranged

explanation.surface: A top-quality touring car has its route planned.
explanation.definitionFit: An air route is a regular path flown by aircraft, a way through the sky.

clue.text: A lady, but to a high degree a beastly mother

parts.note: MA is the Master of Arts, a postgraduate academic degree
a dam is the mother of an animal, such as a horse

explanation.surface: A woman described as an exceptionally brutish parent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To a high degree' reads as 'extremely', but it is the qualification MA.
explanation.definitionFit: Madam is a polite form of address to a woman of standing.
